summary: A short reference from the Refero design skill on icons in product UI. It argues icons should be treated like typography: functional, consistent, and drawn from one set. It gives display sizes by context, stroke weight trade-offs, icon-to-text size pairings, color and contrast rules, accessibility requirements, optical corrections, and a pre-ship checklist. It closes with a table of when to pick Lucide, Heroicons, Phosphor, Material Symbols or SF Symbols. For a design system it supplies concrete defaults for the icon size, stroke and library decisions.
key_ideas: In product UI icons are functional, like type, not decoration
Marketing may use duotone, gradients and illustrative icons, but that style must not leak into the product
Display size depends on context: 16px dense/inline, 20-24px controls, 28-32px feature cards and empty states
Thinner strokes suit larger sizes; thicker strokes hold up better at small sizes
Round caps and joins read friendlier; square ones read technical and precise
Consistency across one library matters more than the specific values
Geometric center is not visual center; play triangles and chevrons need nudging
Aim for equal visual mass across shapes, not equal measurements
Icons default to currentColor so they follow text color and themes
Semantic colors on icons are for status only
Meaningful icons need 3:1 contrast; decorative ones are hidden from assistive tech
Variable glyph systems (Material Symbols, SF Symbols) can match icon weight to text weight

claims.claim: Most icon libraries use a 24x24px canvas, but this is convention, not law.
claims.evidence: Icon Sizing: Most libraries use 24×24px as base

claims.claim: A 2px stroke is the common default in Lucide and Heroicons.
claims.evidence: Stroke weight: Standard (2px): common default in Lucide, Heroicons

claims.claim: Circles look lighter than squares and diagonals look thinner than horizontals at the same stroke.
Mixing icon libraries such as Lucide and Heroicons produces a collage effect.
Semibold text next to a thin icon looks like it comes from different systems.

rules.rule: Use one icon style and one library across the whole product; do not mix outline in nav with solid in buttons and duotone in cards.
rules.why: Mixing styles or libraries reads as a collage.
rules.evidence: Style Consistency: One language per product. No exceptions.

rules.rule: Keep duotone, gradient and illustrative icons in marketing surfaces only, never in product UI.
rules.why: Product icons must be predictable, scalable and themeable.
rules.evidence: Two Contexts: Never leaks into product

rules.rule: Size icons by context: 16px inline with body text, in table cells and dense UI; 20-24px in buttons, nav items and form inputs; 28-32px in feature cards, empty states and marketing.
rules.why: Display size depends on context.

rules.rule: Use a thinner stroke (1.5px) for larger icons and a thicker stroke (2.5px+) for small icons; 2px is the standard default.
rules.why: Thinner feels lighter and works better large; thicker has more presence and holds up small.
rules.evidence: Stroke weight varies by library and style

rules.rule: Choose round caps and joins for a friendly, modern tone, or square ones for a technical, precise tone, to match the product.
rules.why: Caps and joins change the felt tone of the icons.

rules.rule: Do not draw custom icons that ignore the chosen system's grid and stroke.
rules.why: They break the one-language consistency.

rules.rule: Optically center asymmetric icons: shift play triangles right by 0.5-1px and chevrons or arrows toward their point; check by placing the icon in a circle.
rules.why: Geometric center is not visual center.

rules.rule: Balance icons for equal visual mass rather than equal measurements.
rules.why: Circles appear lighter than squares and diagonals thinner than horizontals at the same stroke.

rules.rule: Pair icon size with text size: 16px icons with 14-16px text, 18-20px icons with 16-18px text, 20-24px icons with headings, then adjust by visual testing.
rules.why: Given as a starting point for icon and text pairing.

rules.rule: Align icons with text using align-items: center plus a 0.5-1px manual tweak where needed.
rules.why: The source says icons often need a 0.5-1px manual tweak beyond align-items: center.

rules.rule: Match icon weight to adjacent text weight, or use solid icons next to heavy text.
rules.why: Semibold text with a thin icon looks like it comes from different systems.

rules.rule: Color icons with currentColor by default.
rules.why: It inherits text color and syncs with themes automatically.

rules.rule: Use red, green and amber on icons only to signal error, success and warning status, never as decoration.
rules.why: Semantic colors are for status.

rules.rule: Give meaningful icons, including icon buttons, toggles and status indicators, at least 3:1 contrast.
rules.why: WCAG non-text contrast; applies to icon buttons, toggles and status indicators.

rules.rule: Put an aria-label on icon-only action buttons (or show visible text nearby) and mark decorative icons aria-hidden="true".
rules.why: Accessibility requirements for action vs decorative icons.

rules.rule: Give icon buttons a hit area of 44x44px on touch and 32x32px on desktop, even if the visible icon is smaller.
rules.why: Hit area requirement for icon buttons.

rules.rule: Before shipping, check icons at 50% scale, in grayscale, in dark theme, in table rows, for 3:1 contrast, 44px+ touch targets and same style everywhere.
rules.why: Pre-ship checklist.

rules.rule: With Material Symbols, sync the wght axis with text weight, raise opsz for smaller icons, and toggle FILL between outline (0) and solid (1).
rules.why: Variable glyphs can match text weight dynamically.

rules.rule: Use SF Symbols in SwiftUI/UIKit apps, not on the web.
rules.why: They match San Francisco weight and are a native system.

rules.rule: Pick one icon library or define your own icon spec (canvas, stroke, caps) and hold to it.
rules.why: Consistency matters more than specific values.

rules.rule: If an icon does not read instantly, simplify it.
rules.why: Icons are typography: consistent, optical, accessible.

process.detail: Decide product UI icon style (clean outline or solid, one set) separately from marketing illustration style, and keep the marketing style out of the product.
Choose one library from the When to Use What table, or define your own canvas, stroke and cap spec.
Use context sizes (16 / 20-24 / 28-32px) and the icon-to-text pairing table as a starting point, then adjust visually.
Nudge asymmetric glyphs toward visual center and balance visual mass; test centering inside a circle.
Default to currentColor, reserve semantic colors for status, check 3:1 contrast, add aria-label or aria-hidden, and give hit areas of 44px touch / 32px desktop.
Check 50% scale, grayscale, dark theme, table rows, contrast, touch targets and consistency.
